item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Small on Substance, Big on Pomp
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s fete for his Chinese counterpart President Xi Jinping has been heavy on pageantry and platitudes but light on substantive announcements. The most significant news tied to the gathering materialized before it even began, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides had extended a trade truce for another two months. Anticipated agreements on tariff cuts and a new line of communication on artificial intelligence have yet to surface. Bloomberg's Rebecca Choong Wilkins reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Arabia Ramps Up Oil Exports Via Hormuz
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s crude shipments in September jumped to the highest level since the start of the Iran war. The kingdom ramped up exports via the Strait of Hormuz after an attack on its East-West pipeline. Bloomberg's Anthony di Paola reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Iran Said to Be Exploring Phased Hormuz Deal (Video)
Qatar’s PM on the Iran War ‘Earthquake’
item.description: Amid the US-Israel war with Iran, Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Al Thani says he’s trying to prevent another escalation and broker a lasting peace between bitter enemies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Seeks to Expand Access to Passport Records for Voter Checks
item.description: The US State Department is moving to give state and local officials, as well as potentially some nonprofit organizations, access to passport records to verify voters’ citizenship.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Goes Big on Pomp But Small on Substance
item.description: Donald Trump’s fete for China’s Xi Jinping has been heavy on pageantry and platitudes but light on substantive announcements, with the events shadowed by the US president’s preoccupation with construction projects and personal grievances.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fabian and Mario Parker

item.title: Why Taiwan Is the Most Volatile Issue for US-China Relations
item.description: Wealthy, democratic and strategically located off the Chinese coast, Taiwan has long been the most volatile issue between the US and China.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee and Samson Ellis

item.title: Here’s the Invite List for Trump’s State Dinner With China’s Xi
item.description: President Donald Trump’s state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping brought together senior officials, prominent tech billionaires and heads of some of the US’s most recognizable companies.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Trump to Campaign in Oklahoma, Alabama as Midterms Creep Closer
item.description: President Donald Trump will hold a pair of rallies next week in Oklahoma and Alabama, looking to shore up candidates in what have been reliably Republican states as polls flash warning signs for the GOP.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: New Jersey Governor Sherrill Calls for Her Lieutenant to Resign
item.description: Governor Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey called for the resignation of the state’s lieutenant governor, Dale Caldwell, after an independent investigation found he engaged in sexual harassment and repeatedly violated state ethics rules.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller and Ezra Fieser

item.title: Tech Titans, Trump Fete China’s Xi at Lavish State Dinner
item.description: Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined President Donald Trump for a state dinner honoring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in a demonstration of US technological and financial might.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Kate Sullivan

item.title: Lula to Ban Online Betting, Offer Debt Relief Before Election
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will sign two provisional measures on Friday, one banning online betting and another aimed at renegotiating individual debts, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck

item.title: What Is The Thucydides Trap and Why Did Xi Raise It With Trump?
item.description: When China’s President Xi Jinping met US leader Donald Trump in Washington on Thursday he called for greater cooperation between the two countries to avoid the “Thucydides Trap”. It’s a phrase that sounds academic, but it goes to the heart of Beijing’s ambitions for their relationship. And it’s not the first time Xi has invoked it: he raised the same idea when Trump visited China in May.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Choong Wilkins

item.title: Thai Court Case Risks Election Rerun, Renewed Political Turmoil
item.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s government faces its biggest survival test yet when one of Thailand’s top courts rules Monday on a case that could invalidate the election that brought it to power.
item.dc:creator: Patpicha Tanakasempipat

item.title: Trump, Xi Tout ‘Friendship’ at Lavish Ceremony
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former US Ambassador to China Gary Locke says President Trump's reception of Xi Jinping marks a "remarkable change" in protocol and elevates the Chinese leader's standing at home and abroad. He discusses China's goals for artificial intelligence, the outlook for trade and security agreements, and what could emerge from talks on agriculture, rare earths and a crisis hotline between Washington and Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: CNN, MS NOW, Politico Reporters Regain White House Entry
item.description: Joe Mathieu spoke with Mario Parker at the White House for a special edition of The Debrief. CNN, MS NOW, and Politico reporters returned to the White House after a standoff over press access. Parker says the scene is beginning to look like a typical high-profile summit again, with more reporters on site for Xi’s state visit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gary Locke: State Dinner 'Elevates' Xi's Global Stature
item.description: Former US Ambassador to China Gary Locke says President Trump's reception of Xi Jinping marks a "remarkable change" in protocol and elevates the Chinese leader's standing at home and abroad. He discusses China's goals for artificial intelligence, the outlook for trade and security agreements, and what could emerge from talks on agriculture, rare earths and a crisis hotline between Washington and Beijing. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: US-China AI Arms Race (Podcast)
item.description:
Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping addressed their intense competition over artificial intelligence on Thursday during a summit aimed at keeping ties between the world’s largest economies on track. How the leaders are handling AI is one of the key questions looming over the state visit, with the US president arguing for unfettered development to keep his nation’s edge. China, meanwhile, has criticized American export controls on semiconductors and other inputs that it argues constrains its companies. By contrast, China’s top leader indicated some openness to setting boundaries.
On today's episode:
Michael Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Technology & Strategic Industries NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte Dina Esfandiary, Middle East Geoeconomics Lead for Bloomberg Economics Eric Muhlheim, Mozilla CFO & Nina Trentmann, Bloomberg News CFO Briefing Editor (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Iran Said to Be Exploring Phased Deal to Open Hormuz
item.description: US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased deal that would see Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lift its blockade of Iranian ports, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald

item.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protesters Target Election Chief Next
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that spearheaded one of India’s biggest student protests in years, on Thursday demanded the resignation of the country’s chief election commissioner within 48 hours, threatening fresh protests if he does not step down.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava
